basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models issued claims with issuer, subject and holder roles, not the authorization they may evidence.
Distinguishes holder from subject and issuer, so custody gives no rights over content.
Keeps issued claims immutable and records changes as events and status updates.
Separates authenticity, current status, issuer authority and claim truth.

may: Verify a credential signature and status against the issuer's published material.
Derive a presentation with only the requested claims.
Refresh status lists when an issuer publishes updates.
Map a credential between formats and note fields lost.
mustNot: Issue a credential without the issuer's authority.
Edit claims in an issued credential instead of issuing a new one.
Present more claims than a verifier requested and the holder allowed.
Treat a valid credential as proof that the claim is true or that the holder is the subject.
Use a licence credential in place of the underlying permit grant.
requiresHuman: Defining a new credential class or trust framework.
Holder consent to a presentation request.

considerations: Credentials gate access to work, travel and services, so wrongful revocation can cause real harm.
Selective disclosure protects privacy; verifiers should not demand full credentials.
Status checks can reveal where and when a holder uses a credential.

items: A credential has an issuer, a subject, claims, an issuance date, a validity period and a proof.
It is confused with the underlying permit or right, an identity record or an access token.
Forged or replayed credentials accepted as valid.
Stale status letting revoked credentials pass.
OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance and Presentations.
